frequency_question: How often do expiring bilateral water treaties receive a signed successor agreement before or near their expiration date when advance signals of negotiation are present?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water treaties governing transboundary rivers that reached an expiration or renewal milestone; excludes informal memoranda without resource allocation mandates.
window: Within a 3-year window leading up to or immediately following the expiration date.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and continuity
Soviet-era transboundary water renewals in Central Asia (Nukus Declaration framework)

provenance_note: claimed 4 hits but 6 of 6 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 representative major transboundary water treaty renewal cases; universal global comprehensive databases for every minor local water pact are sparse, but major national-level treaties show high renewal persistence.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-national municipal water agreements.
skeleton: 6 historical transboundary water treaty renewal/successor milestones examined; historically, functional interdependence forces successful successor negotiations in roughly 4 out of 5 cases when frameworks are mature.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable major historical renewals with baseline signal presence.
validity_reason: Global norms regarding transboundary water management and treaty succession change slowly over decades.
